card.intuition: Next-token prediction is the model's only mode of operation: given a context it samples one next token, appends it, and runs again — every sentence, tool call, or thousand-line file is built one token at a time. The sampling step is why the same prompt can produce different output on different runs.
card.analogy: An autocomplete that types a whole essay one word at a time by always asking 'what likely follows?' — it never checks truth, only likelihood, and it commits to each word as it goes.
card.time_complexity: Generation is strictly sequential — one token per step — so total output time is output_tokens times tokens-per-second, which puts a floor on how fast any agent can work.
card.space_complexity: Each step re-runs the growing context window, so the loop's working set is the tokens accumulated so far, competing for the fixed context budget.
when_to_use: Explaining how a tool-call 'decision' is just a structured string the harness parses out of the output stream
Reasoning about why generation speed caps agent throughput
Explaining hallucination as emitting likely tokens rather than true ones
gotchas: The model never checks whether a token is true, only whether it's likely — the root of hallucination
A confident-sounding opening can steer the rest of the answer wrong because it commits one token at a time

steps.label: Context
steps.annotation: The tokens in the context window run through the parameters.

steps.label: Score
steps.annotation: The model assigns a probability to every token in the vocabulary.

steps.label: Sample
steps.annotation: One token is sampled from those probabilities.

steps.label: Append
steps.annotation: The sampled token is appended and the loop runs again.

steps.label: Emit
steps.annotation: The output stream accumulates until the whole answer is built.

exercise.prompt: Show that output is built one token at a time: autocomplete() walks a chain of next-token lookups and joins the accumulated tokens into a sentence.
hints: Each step looks up the most recent emitted token in the chain table
Use a dictionary lookup with '?' as the stop token when the chain ends
exercise.test_code:
chain = {"cat": "sat", "sat": "down"}
assert autocomplete("cat", chain, 3) == "cat sat down"
assert autocomplete("cat", chain, 1) == "cat"
